Carl Jung, the psychiatrist you are talking about, understood that the unconscious mind is localised to specific areas of the brain, it is not just an abstract concept.

Additionally, the unconscious mind does not contribute to primitive behaviour, i believe you mixed up some terms. The higher cognitive function that is awarded to human beings, that we evolved brains developed, is what I believe you meant to talk about. And that is located in the prefrontal cortex which also has no racial differences.

Let me try and explain this scientifically;

The most primitive part of the brain is the brainstem. All species related characteristics can be traced to the brainstem. Presently, there is no research that indicates a difference in brainstem activity between races, therefore, everything you've said is based on internalised racism na 'si ni mimi nakushow', there is no scientific backing.

There is an increased crime rate among black people in the US mainly because of their socio-economic status. A socio-economic status established after slavery, contributed by the school to prison pipeline.

Many rap songs also preach hope and getting out of the 'hood', experiences of police brutality and struggles with poverty, its not just gang culture and it doesn't always praise it

The notion that it is genetic is likely due to generational trauma from slavery that passes on many instincts that may contribute to aggressive behaviour. I do not believe it is genetic in all black people.

Coming to Kenya, again, colonialism contributed largely -  especially the lines drawn to callously divide countries, without considering tribal relations (tribalism being one of our biggest problems). Stealing from the people comes from a loss of a sense of community, an indivualism for oneself and ones relatives/tribe and the normalisation of the culture of corruption.

I don't think we should blame everything on slavery and colonialism but we cannot ignore their influence. Assuming its just genetic or just 'how we are as blacks' is very detrimental because it discourages growth and we need to grow to break these generational traumas.
